A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OMEGA and its adversarial extension. The main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing relocated and renumbered material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original scene-generation experiments, guidance comparisons, ablations and a synthetic toy experiment, including additional results in Appendix E.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds planner-specific adversarial evaluations, WOSAC results and a phase-specific guidance ablation.

M1.justification: V3 extends adversarial generation by incorporating an ego planner's trajectory through weak-noise partial masking (Sections 4.3 and D.2). The optimization, SE-IBR and underlying two-phase procedure remain unchanged. Phase-specific guidance, now emphasized as a phase-aligned schedule, was already described in v1 Section C.3.

E1.justification: V3 substantially extends adversarial task coverage from jointly generated ego-attacker behavior to planner-specific attacks involving Replay, constant-velocity and IDM planners (Table 3). Existing nuPlan, Waymo, goal-conditioned and toy coverage remains. The additional WOSAC evaluation reuses the Waymo domain.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain Diffusion Policy, SceneDiffuser, Nexus, GHC/CTG/DPS guidance and Nexus-FT/GC/CTGAdv adversarial variants. WOSAC compares against the existing Nexus baseline. Replay, constant velocity and IDM serve as targets of the new adversarial evaluation rather than competing scene generators.

E3.justification: V3 adds WOSAC evaluation using one second of history, 32 stochastic futures, interpolation from 2 Hz outputs to 10 Hz, and the Realism Meta score. It also adds planner-conditioned testing with scene-minimum TTC and at-fault/non-at-fault collision statistics. The existing 4,096-scenario, four-sample evaluations and 100 goal-conditioned cases retain their settings.

E4.justification: V3 Table 4 adds an ablation removing phase-specific guidance, reporting 33.47% scene validity versus 72.27% for the full method. It removes v1 Appendix E.1's detailed speed-conditioned acceleration, jerk and yaw-rate analysis and Figure A1. Existing phase/KL ablations, toy analysis and failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or variability across repeated experimental runs. WOSAC's 32 generated futures constitute a sampling protocol, not newly reported statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: V3 adds WOSAC scores of 0.6095 for Nexus and 0.7001 for Nexus-OMEGA, planner-specific outcomes in Table 3, and the phase-guidance ablation. Matched guidance/ablation tables revise no-KL validity from 63.40% to 18.21% and full-method speed JSD from 0.433 to 0.333, resolving its discrepancy with Table 1. Headline benchmark, goal-conditioned and generic adversarial scores remain unchanged. Detailed appendix kinematic distributions are removed.

T1.justification: The optimization and sensitivity equations, Appendix A derivations and assumptions, and Appendix C constraint definitions are retained. Revised explanations do not introduce new proofs or substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of training-free re-anchoring, two-phase interaction refinement and sensitivity-based adversarial generation, including the same headline numerical improvements. The scheduling contribution is reframed without changing its underlying scientific scope.

C2.justification: V3 softens the toy experiment's interpretation from preserving distribution structure and remaining within high-density regions to largely preserving modes and limiting drift. It adds explanations of conflicting early interaction guidance, planner-relevant failures, and WOSAC's limitations concerning annotation artifacts and distribution matching. The runtime limitation and four existing failure cases remain.

D1.justification: V3 documents interpolation of 2 Hz outputs for WOSAC and incorporation of planned ego trajectories through noise-based partial masking. Existing backbone checkpoints, constraint implementation and project access information remain unchanged; the expanded scheduling description largely restates details already present in v1.

R1.justification: V3 adds references including Diffusion Forcing, MDG and language-guided traffic simulation, and expands positioning against noise-modulation approaches. It also cites a critique of WOSAC to motivate metric choice. The central positioning against existing diffusion guidance and adversarial generators remains.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in related work, scheduling explanations and Appendix B's toy discussion. The schedule is renamed, author text is corrected, and former Appendix E material is consolidated into Appendix D. The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column format. Figure 4 is substantially redrawn; a planner-results table and WOSAC visualization are added. Full v1 appendix tables are consolidated into main Tables 2 and 4, while the detailed kinematic Figure A1 is removed. Retained qualitative grids are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: WOSAC results, tests with three simple ego planners and the phase-guidance ablation strengthen empirical support. Revised table values resolve inconsistencies, and the more qualified manifold discussion improves precision. Removing detailed kinematic plots sacrifices diagnostic depth, but the added validation and reporting corrections provide a modest net improvement to the largely retained work.
